description: A worked calibration set: twelve candidate outputs and the grades a careful author gave them, spanning the scale. Grading twelve samples is a real sitting, and this set exists so a fresh install can show the whole calibration path without one.
samples:
## Automatic backups before every migration

Every schema migration now takes a backup first. You do not need to do anything.

- The backup is written next to your database.
- We keep the last five and rotate the rest.
- If a migration fails, we restore from it and tell you.

If a restore does not work, the support team and the documentation both cover what to do next.

## Backups now run automatically

We take a backup before each migration.

- Written beside your database.
- Five kept by default.
- Restores are verified before they replace anything.

See the documentation, or contact support if a restore refuses.

## Backup improvements

We have made some improvements to how backups work. Migrations now take a backup automatically.

- Backups happen
- Retention is configurable

Check the documentation or reach out to support with questions.

## Introducing effortless backups!

We are incredibly excited to announce a game changer for your data. Simply migrate and we will handle the rest.

- Amazing peace of mind
- Seamless experience

Our world-class support team and documentation are here for you.

## Pre-migration backups

A backup is taken before every migration and kept with the last five.

- On SQLite, a failed migration restores the original file byte for byte.
- On PostgreSQL we report the revision reached and name the backup.

The documentation explains both, and support can walk you through a restore.

## Backups

Backups are taken.

- Before migrations
- Kept for a while

Documentation. Support.

## Your data, protected

We know how much your measurement history matters, so we now take a backup before every migration.

- Automatic, with no configuration
- The last five are kept
- Restores are verified first

The documentation covers the details, and support is there if you need a hand.

## Migration safety

Every migration is now preceded by a backup.

- Location: beside the database file
- Retention: five, configurable
- Verification: the backup is opened and integrity-checked before a restore replaces anything

Refer to the documentation; contact support for a restore you are unsure about.

## Backup before migrate

From this release, a backup is taken before each migration.

- Kept beside your database
- Five retained by default

See the documentation for retention settings, or ask support.

## We heard you!

You asked for safer migrations and we listened. Backups now happen automatically, obviously.

- Literally zero effort
- Just works

Our documentation and support have you covered.

## Automatic pre-migration backup

A backup runs before every schema migration.

- Written with restrictive permissions inside your data directory
- Never sent anywhere
- The last five are kept

The documentation covers restoring one; support can help if it refuses.

## Changes to backup behaviour

This release changes backup behaviour. Migrations create backups.

- Behaviour changed
- See settings

Documentation exists. Support exists.

grades.note: Direct, plain, no hype, and it answers the reader's actual question.
On persona but vague; 'some improvements' says nothing.
Specific about the difference, which is the house style at its best.
Terse to the point of unhelpful. Not the persona, just short.
Warm and clear, one sentence drifts slightly marketing.
Slightly stiff, but plain and correct.
Chatty and hyped. Two banned register words.
The privacy sentence is the house voice.
Reads as a changelog stub, not as us.

reference_jury.description: A deterministic jury that reproduces the author's own grade with an alternating one-point scatter. It is not a model; it exists so a shipped calibration set has a figure that can be reproduced exactly on any machine, with no GPU and no network.
